d:
Month stepper at the top of the Mes view.

The arrows are the only way to change month — there is no date picker here, because the app is built around one month at a time and jumping is rare.

Prev is disabled in January and next in December: the store holds one calendar year, so there is nowhere to step to. Touch targets are 44px on mobile and 32px on desktop.

Desktop adds the “Agregar” popover, which carries the same three actions the FAB carries on mobile. Title is Heading/Subsection — the code had 17px bold, snapped to the 18px scale step.

Full-height navigation panel. The panel itself is square (radius/none) — it is flush to the viewport edge, so a corner radius there would read as a floating card, which it is not. The rows are menu-item instances (radius/16 on a 40px row).

One crumb. Type=Link is navigable; Type=Current is the current page, marked with aria-current, and therefore only exists in State=Default — it does not react to the pointer and does not take focus.

State documents the link states: Default, Hover (underline plus a darker foreground), Focus (a 2px ring drawn outside, over the 4px padding that exists precisely to house it).

The 4px padding-x is not decoration: it is the box of the focus ring. Removing it makes the ring cut through the letters.

Hierarchical navigation between pages. The last crumb is the current page and is not a link.

Levels = how many crumbs are shown. More than 4 is not supported: if the path is deeper, collapse the middle segments before reaching this component — the breadcrumb does not truncate on its own.

The house icon lives in the first crumb and is off by default, because only the root carries it.

Tokens: breadcrumb/* in the Component collection, all aliases, both modes.
A single bottom-nav tab.
Mobile tab bar, 412×58. The FAB with its speed-dial sits above it, not inside it.

A sidebar row. State × Expanded.

40px tall, 12px radius, px-3 py-2 expanded and p-3 centred when collapsed.

Selected is cyan. Hover stays neutral on purpose: two cyan states next to each other read as two selections.

Naming nit, still open: the State values mix casing (Selected | default | disabled | hover).

The onboarding wizard rail. It reports progress AND what has been chosen so far, because in a three-step flow where every step is optional and pre-filled, “how far along am I” is a weak question — the answer is always “almost done” — and “what am I actually keeping” is the useful one.

That second line matters in Neto specifically: the flow lets you skip any step. A rail that shows the value makes the consequence visible.

State is carried by silhouette, not only by hue: Done is filled with a check, Current is a ring with a solid dot, Pending is an empty ring. Colour alone would leave Current and Pending indistinguishable to anyone who cannot separate the two tints. The connector line is the redundant encoding of the same progress — not decoration.

Desktop only. On mobile the bar stays: no room for a rail, and none for the value line either.

One step of the onboarding stepper. Done is interactive — you can go back — which is why it alone has a hover; Current and Pending are not.

Show Connector is false on the last item only. The connector belongs to the item rather than the parent so the stepper can wrap without leaving a line pointing at nothing.

The Mes view tab strip, composed of Tab instances.

Its length is variable: Tributarias and Provisiones only exist when the user has those deduction groups enabled.

Header bar, 54px.

Holds the live TRM chip, the notification bell, the theme toggle and the account menu. Configuración and Perfil live in that menu, not in the main navigation — which is why the nav shows four destinations for five surfaces.

Floating panel anchored to a trigger. 288px wide.

Desktop only — on mobile the same content opens in a Sheet, because a popover near the bottom of a phone screen ends up under the thumb or off-screen.

Uses bg/anchored, which is a separate elevation rung from the card surface, so a popover over a card still reads as a layer above it.

Short explanation on hover or focus. Side = where it sits relative to the trigger, which is also where the arrow points.

Inverts against the page — bg/inverse with fg/on-inverse — so it reads as an overlay and never as part of the content underneath.

Desktop only: there is no hover on touch. Anything a mobile user needs to know must be visible without one.

Mobile action menu for a list row.

Deleting takes two taps and the sheet stays open between them: the first tap turns the row red and rewrites it to “Tocar para confirmar eliminación”. There is no modal — the confirmation happens in place, so the user never loses sight of which entry they are deleting.

Desktop uses inline row actions instead; this component does not appear there.

The panel every form opens in. Device × Footer, plus a Content instance-swap slot.

Mobile slides up from the bottom with a drag handle and rounds its top corners. Desktop slides in from the right and rounds only the left side. Different patterns, not a reflow — that is why Device is a variant and not a breakpoint.

The scrim behind it is bg/scrim and is not part of this component. On mobile the sheet is clamped to the visual viewport so the keyboard never covers the fields.

Content was added 2026-08-21. Before it, the body held a text node and an instance cannot have children added or removed, so every flow that needed a real form had to detach the sheet.

The default occupant of Sheet’s Content slot. Swap it for the real form. It exists so Sheet has something to swap: an instance-swap property needs a component as its default, and a bare text node cannot be one.

The colour section of the account edit drawer — the part that feature adds, not the whole form. Name, type, currency, number and balance already exist above it in code and are not redrawn here.

Two things it fixes in place: the live AccountAvatar shows what the choice produces, so the picker chips do not have to preview the tint themselves; and the picker is wrapped in Field, so its label comes from the same place every other label in Neto does.
User avatar, SM–XL. Falls back to initials on the avatar/background token when there is no image.

Sized wrapper around a Lucide glyph. size = XS 12 · S 16 · M 20 · L 24, bound to icon-size/*.

The glyph itself is the Glyph property — an instance swap wired to the 76 icons on the Icons page. Change the glyph there, never by detaching.

Every icon in the product goes through this component, which is why size is a variant and not a manual resize: an icon at 17px is a bug, not a choice.
Account-type glyph. One variant per account type, so the icon can never disagree with the account type it sits next to.

An account’s identity mark: the tinted circle in account/{hue}/surface with the account-type glyph in account/{hue}/accent. This is the pairing the colour picker chooses, and the only place the surface token is used.

The account TYPE stays a nested Icon Account swap rather than a variant axis. Twelve colours times four types would be 48 variants for two decisions that belong to different people: the colour is the user’s, the type is the account’s.

Glyph contrast verified against its own tint in both modes — a filled glyph is a graphic object (WCAG 1.4.11), the rule the favourite star was got wrong on.

Ordered by hue angle: orange 21° · amber 32 · lime 86 · green 142 · emerald 161 · teal 175 · sky 200 · blue 221 · indigo 243 · purple 271 · pink 333 · rose 347. The neighbours are the pairs that measure closest, which is what lets someone see they are two colours.

The tinted bubble that opens every ledger row: a 32px circle in a subtle background token with a 16px glyph in the matching foreground token. Six types, one nested swap — putting them on LedgerRow instead would multiply every row state by six for a decision the entry already carries.

Two glyphs do double duty. income and transfer-in share arrow-down-left; egreso and transfer-out share arrow-up-right. Colour is the only thing separating each pair inside the bubble, so it is never the only carrier in use: the row prints “Desde {cuenta}” or “Hacia {cuenta}” for a transfer and the entry description for the rest (WCAG 1.4.1).

scheduled OVERRIDES the type rather than sitting beside it. A scheduled entry shows the clock on the neutral tint whatever it is underneath, because at that point what matters is that it has not happened yet. The row also drops to 60% and prints the “Programado” badge.

Glyph contrast is measured against its own tint in both modes: Light floor 3.58:1 (income), Dark floor 5.84:1 (egreso). A filled glyph is a graphic object, so 1.4.11 applies.

The glyph is 16 (icon-size/md), not the 14 the code passes. 14 is not a rung on the icon scale — 12 · 16 · 20 · 24 — and a one-off would flatten the scale for one row.

OPEN for Dev: the ss bubble in code paints its glyph with --color-tax, which resolves to bg/tax (amber/400) and measures 1.61:1 on amber/50 in Light. That fails 1.4.11. Figma uses fg/tax (amber/700, 4.84:1); the published name is --color-tax-txt.

The Gastos tab — the largest container in the system: category chips with counts, sort and filters, and a distribution bar.

The strip of category chips only renders categories that have data that month, so its length changes month to month and the layout has to survive one chip or fifteen.

The Ingresos tab of the Mes view.

Lists the month’s incomes with account badges and a gross total converted with that month’s TRM.

The Provisiones tab: primas, cesantías, vacaciones, computed on gross income with provisions enabled.

Conditional in the same way as TaxContainer. Users can add their own provisions, so the list length is not fixed.

The Tributarias tab: salud, pensión, ARL and retención, plus the FSS row that appears automatically when IBC ≥ 4 SMMLV.

Conditional — the whole tab is absent for the empleado profile. Also holds the payment calendar keyed to the last digits of the cédula.
The Movimientos tab. Transfers between own accounts, with the effective-TRM calculator.

The Neto mark. Style=Primary is the mark on its brand ground; Style=Secondary is the reversed treatment for dark or photographic backgrounds.

Bound to logo/mark and logo/bg, which hold the SAME value in light and dark on purpose: a logo that changes colour with the theme is a different logo. This is identity, not a semantic colour, and it is the one place in the system where mode-invariance is the point.

Google mark, used on the sign-in button. Its four colours are Google’s, not ours: they are raw hexes ON PURPOSE and must never be bound to a token, because a token implies we are allowed to change them and we are not. They have no dark mode either — the mark is the same in both, which is also why it sits on Brand and not in the Icon Library. Exempt from C1 by CONFIG.foreignBrand; see design-system/docs/16-marks.md. The GitHub mark is the opposite case and is a normal glyph: monochrome, inherits currentColor.

Country flag, used to recognise a currency at a glance. Its colours belong to a state, not to us: they stay raw on purpose and must never be tokenised, exactly like the Google mark. The brand-mark/ prefix is what makes C1 skip them by configuration rather than by anyone remembering (design-system/docs/16-marks.md).
